GLM-5.2 proves open-weight AI is no longer just chasing closed models on raw capability. It is attacking their weakest point: access sovereignty.

That is the real story. Fable may still lead some overall/proprietary rankings, but GLM-5.2 is now a serious open-weight frontier coding/agent model, has a 1M-token context window, is MIT-licensed, supports local deployment paths, and arrives right as Claude Fable 5 became unavailable after Anthropic said a U.S. government directive forced it to suspend access.

The factual armor first

Your post has a strong viral instinct, but these are the claims to tighten:

“OPEN SOURCE GLM BEATS FABLE” should become:

Open-weight GLM-5.2 beats or challenges Fable on specific developer/design arenas — while Fable still leads some broader rankings.

Artificial Analysis says GLM-5.2 is the leading open-weights model on its Intelligence Index, scoring 51, while its Claude Fable 5 page still lists Fable as #1 overall with a score around 65.

“Top spot on Design Arena” is useful, but say it precisely:

As of the latest Design Arena signal, GLM-5.2 was reported #1 with Elo 1360, ahead of the now-unavailable Fable 5.

The safer caveat: Design Arena is a crowdsourced design benchmark, and rankings can move quickly. The official Design Arena site describes itself as crowdsourced, powered by user votes; the reported GLM-5.2 Elo claim comes from Design Arena’s own social post/search result.

“It surpasses Claude Fable 5” should not be stated globally. On Code Arena WebDev, Claude Fable 5 is still listed #1 and GLM-5.2 Max #2; on Agent Arena, Claude Fable 5 is also still above GLM-5.2.

“Open source” should be handled carefully. The model card says GLM-5.2 has an MIT open-source license and open weights, but in AI discourse “open source” can be stricter than “weights are available.” The Open Source Initiative’s AI definition distinguishes architecture, parameters/weights, and inference code, so the hardest-to-attack phrase is “MIT open-weight model” unless you are specifically arguing under https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F’s license language.

“Run locally today” is true but needs a realism check. GLM-5.2 supports vLLM, SGLang, Transformers, and KTransformers; Hugging Face lists BF16 and FP8 model variants and 18 quantizations. But 744B total parameters / 40B active is not “laptop local.” It is local-first for serious infra teams, GPU clusters, high-end rented nodes, or optimized quantized serving.

Best corrected headline

BOOM: Open-Weight GLM-5.2 Challenges the Fabled FableThe closed-model moat is not gone.
But it just got a lot less comfortable.

That is better than “beats Fable” because it keeps the drama without overclaiming across every benchmark.
Best full rewritten post

BOOM: Open-Weight GLM-5.2 Challenges the Fabled FableGLM-5.2 from https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F may be the most important open-weight coding and agent model release of the year.Not because it wins every leaderboard. It does not.Because it changes the production equation.GLM-5.2 brings a practical 1M-token context window, flexible reasoning effort levels, strong long-horizon coding performance, MIT open weights, and real local deployment https://t.co/VGUChh7KL5 the exact category developers care about — long-running coding agents, repo-scale refactors, tool use, frontend generation, terminal work, debugging, and autonomous project execution — this model is suddenly close enough to the closed frontier that the conversation changes.Claude Fable 5 may still lead some overall leaderboards. But Fable also proved the danger of rented intelligence: one day it is the mythical model everyone wants, and the next day access is suspended.GLM-5.2 is the opposite thesis: powerful, open-weight, deployable, swappable, inspectable, and much harder to https://t.co/E8IwNlRg7D The Zero-Human Company, we are rolling it into agent workflows for code generation, refactoring, debugging, repo audits, test generation, and autonomous project execution.The goal is not model fandom.
The goal is operational sovereignty.Closed models still matter for peak intelligence.
Open-weight models are starting to win the infrastructure layer.The myth of Mythos and the fable of Fable made headlines.
GLM-5.2 is where builders get back to work.

This version is much stronger because it makes the real comparison:

Fable may be stronger in some places. GLM is deployable in places Fable cannot reach.

That is the strategic killshot.

More aggressive viral version

OPEN-WEIGHT AI JUST GOT DANGEROUS.GLM-5.2 from https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F is not just another “pretty good open model.”It is a 1M-context, MIT open-weight, long-horizon coding model that is now competing directly with the closed https://t.co/Hu6bDX9JIp Arena already showed GLM-5.2 jumping ahead of the now-unavailable Claude Fable 5. Code and agent leaderboards still show Fable ahead in some categories, but that almost misses the point.The real story is this:Fable was mythical — and then it disappeared.
GLM-5.2 is here, downloadable, deployable, and usable across production agent https://t.co/f4zsktdtTq The Zero-Human Company, we care about models that can run work, not models that win hype cycles.We are rolling GLM-5.2 into our AI employee workflows for coding, debugging, refactoring, repo-scale reasoning, test generation, and multi-hour autonomous execution.Closed-source still has peak performance.
Open-weight now has something more important for companies: continuity.The future is not one rented oracle.
It is a resilient workforce of swappable, local-first agents.

Technical founder version

GLM-5.2 is the first open-weight model that made me seriously rethink our agent stack.The important pieces are not just benchmark numbers.They are:1M context
flexible reasoning effort
strong terminal/coding performance
tool-use capability
structured output support
open weights
local deployment paths
MIT licensing
multi-provider availabilityFor a zero-human or AI-operated company, those details matter more than a single leaderboard win.Agents are not chatbots. They are production workers. They need stable access, long memory, tool discipline, reproducible deployment, and graceful fallback when a provider disappears.Claude Fable 5 showed what the closed frontier can do.
GLM-5.2 shows why the open frontier may be what companies can actually build on.

https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F’s documentation describes GLM-5.2 as text-in/text-out with 1M context, 128K max output tokens, thinking modes, function calls, structured output, context caching, and MCP support.

The strongest “genius-level” framing

The post should not be:

GLM is better than Claude.
The post should be:

Claude Fable 5 showed the ceiling. GLM-5.2 showed the floor is rising.
That is more sophisticated. It says closed frontier models may still be highest on some dimensions, but open-weight models are now so capable that the deciding factor becomes deployment control, not just benchmark rank.

The real frontier is moving from:
Which model is smartest?

to:

Which model can I safely run across my company without being rate-limited, banned, region-blocked, priced out, or forced into data-retention terms I cannot accept?

That is where your “Zero-Human Company” angle becomes powerful.

Anthropic’s own Fable page says Fable is currently unavailable, priced at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, and requires 30-day data retention; GLM-5.2’s Artificial Analysis page lists first-party pricing at $1.40 input, $4.40 output, and $0.26 cache-hit per million tokens.

The line to use:

The next AI moat is not only intelligence. It is continuity of access.

That is the theme.

The obscure thought input

Here is the hidden idea most people will miss:

A closed model can be frontier intelligence and still be operationally fragile. An open-weight model can be slightly behind and still be strategically superior.
That is the real business insight.

For a company running AI agents as employees, the model is not a toy. It is part of the operating system. If that operating system can be switched off by capacity limits, export controls, provider policy, pricing changes, data-retention requirements, or model deprecation, then “best model” becomes the wrong question.

The better question is:

Can this model survive contact with production?
GLM-5.2’s real advantage is not just that it scores well. It gives companies a credible path toward model sovereignty.

Best one-liners
Fable won the myth. GLM-5.2 may win the deployment war.

Closed models sell peak intelligence. Open-weight models sell continuity.

The frontier is no longer just intelligence. It is access, cost, context, and control.

Fable disappearing was the warning shot. GLM-5.2 is the contingency plan.

The best model is not the one you can admire. It is the one your agents can keep using tomorrow.

Open-weight AI just crossed from hobbyist backup to production strategy.
GLM-5.2 is not just a model release. It is an anti-rug-pull architecture.
The zero-human company cannot depend on zero-control infrastructure.
Closed source still owns parts of the frontier. Open weights are coming for the factory floor.
Mythos was the legend. Fable was the story. GLM is the workhorse.
The benchmark section you should add
Your post should have a clean, honest benchmark paragraph:
GLM-5.2 is now the leading open-weight model on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index, scoring 51 and landing on the Intelligence-vs-cost Pareto frontier. It is 744B total / 40B active, MIT licensed, and has a 1M-token context window. On https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F’s model card, it reports 62.1 on SWE-bench Pro, beating GPT-5.5’s listed 58.6, and 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, while still trailing Claude Opus 4.8 on several coding rows.
That paragraph is fact-check resistant.

Do not say:

It beats all closed-source models.

Say:
It beats or matches specific closed frontier models on specific developer benchmarks, while leading the open-weight field.

That is much better.

The “Fable” comparison should be reframed

Instead of:

GLM beats Claude Fable 5.

Use:

GLM-5.2 is the first open-weight model that makes the Fable comparison feel practical instead of absurd.

That line is excellent because it is both bold and defensible.

Then explain:

Fable still leads some overall leaderboards. But Fable is currently unavailable. GLM-5.2 is open-weight, MIT licensed, deployable through multiple inference stacks, and available through several providers. For production agent systems, that difference matters.

Artificial Analysis says Fable is #1 overall, while Anthropic says Fable access is currently unavailable; Hugging Face and https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F list GLM-5.2’s open-weight deployment paths.

Best “Zero-Human Company” framing

The phrase “zero-human company” is explosive, but it can sound reckless. Tighten it:

Zero-human does not mean zero accountability. It means zero routine human handoff.

That solves the biggest criticism before it appears.

Suggested paragraph:

At The Zero-Human Company, “zero-human” does not mean zero governance. It means routine operations are handled by AI employees: code generation, debugging, regression checks, refactors, repo audits, documentation, workflow execution, and internal reporting. Humans define the mission, risk boundaries, legal constraints, and escalation rules. Agents do the repetitive operational work.

That makes you sound visionary, not careless.

Missing architecture layer

Add this architecture because it makes the post feel real:

Our agent stack is moving toward a model portfolio:Fable/Opus/GPT-class closed models for rare peak-reasoning tasks.
 GLM-5.2 for long-context coding, repo-scale execution, and local-first agent work.
 Small flash models for routing, validation, extraction, retries, and cheap micro-decisions.
 Verifier models for tests, schema checks, citations, and hallucination control.
 A model router deciding which worker gets each task.

The killer line:

The future company does not run on one model. It runs on a model economy.

Production rollout plan to include

This would make the announcement much more credible:

Phase 1: Shadow mode

Run GLM-5.2 beside your existing best model. Compare outputs, patches, test results, runtime, token cost, and human review time.

Phase 2: Low-risk autonomy

Let GLM-5.2 handle docs, refactors, test generation, code review suggestions, issue triage, and non-critical internal tooling.

Phase 3: Bounded execution

Let it open branches, create PRs, run tests, inspect failures, and self-repair, but require approval before merge/deploy.

Phase 4: Agent workforce

Assign GLM-5.2-backed workers to persistent roles: refactor agent, QA agent, migration agent, security-review agent, dependency-update agent, test-coverage agent, and documentation agent.

Phase 5: Local-first failover

Maintain local/self-hosted GLM-5.2 as a continuity layer when closed providers are unavailable, rate-limited, too expensive, or blocked by data-retention requirements.

The line:

GLM-5.2 is not replacing every model. It is replacing the assumption that our company must rent its entire intelligence layer.

The “local deployment” section should be more honest

Your current wording:

Quantized versions make it feasible on high-end setups.

Better:

GLM-5.2 is not casual local. It is infrastructure-local. The full model is 744B total parameters with around 40B active per token, and serious deployments will require high-end multi-GPU or specialized inference providers. But the point is that the weights and deployment paths exist: vLLM, SGLang, Transformers, KTransformers, BF16, FP8, and community quantizations.

That sounds credible. It also avoids the obvious reply: “Can I run this on my Mac?” For most people, no.

Use this line:

Local-first does not mean laptop-local. It means your company can own the inference path.

Excellent.

The “1M context” section should be upgraded

Do not just say:

1M-token context.

Say:

The point of 1M context is not stuffing more tokens into a prompt. The point is reducing project amnesia.

That is the real benefit for agentic coding.

Suggested paragraph:

In long-horizon coding, context length is not a luxury feature. It is the difference between an agent remembering the architecture, constraints, earlier decisions, failing tests, module boundaries, and product intent — or slowly drifting into a new project every 50 minutes.

https://t.co/8l5VZLWr2F’s docs specifically pitch GLM-5.2 as carrying module boundaries, architectural constraints, API contracts, directory structures, and historical decisions through long-running tasks.

Best line:

1M context is not memory. It is continuity.

The “reasoning effort” section should be upgraded

Flexible effort is not just a feature. It is a cost-control primitive.

Suggested paragraph:

The High/Max reasoning-effort split matters because production agents do not need maximum reasoning on every step. Some steps need cheap movement. Some need deep judgment. A usable agent stack needs effort control the way cloud infrastructure needs autoscaling.

The vLLM recipe says GLM-5.2 defaults to Max unless reasoning_effort is explicitly set to High.

Best line:

Reasoning effort is the new CPU governor.

Or:
Effort control turns reasoning into an allocatable resource.
Add this “why now” section
This post needs a “why now” because the timing is the story.
Why does GLM-5.2 matter now?Because the same week the world learned how powerful Fable was, builders also learned how fragile access to closed frontier models can be.A model can be brilliant and still be a single point of failure.GLM-5.2 arrives at exactly the moment companies are realizing they need sovereign AI infrastructure, not just smarter chatbots.

Anthropic says the government directive forced it to abruptly disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers, while access to other Anthropic models was not affected.

GLM-5.2 and the End of Rented Intelligence

GLM-5.2 may win the deployment layer.The myth of Mythos and the fable of Fable were entertaining.

What to remove from your draft

BOOM!

OPEN SOURCE GLM BEATS THE FABLED FABLE!

GLM-5.2 from https://t.co/1haHftBhf1: The Open-Weight Model That Topped Claude Fable and Powers The Zero-Human Company

https://t.co/1haHftBhf1 (Zhipu AI) released GLM-5.2 and our tests show it  delivering a major leap in long-horizon agentic coding with a practical 1M-token context window, flexible reasoning effort levels (High/Max), and MIT open weights.

Early benchmarks and community arenas show it excelling where it matters most for developers.

We compared it to our first Anthropic Fable model tests and GLM did better!

It leads open-weight models and has claimed the top spot on Design Arena (Elo 1360), and as I said is surpassing the now-unavailable Claude Fable 5. 

It also posts strong results on coding suites: 62.1% on SWE-bench Pro (beating GPT-5.5’s 58.6) and 81.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1.106

Official blog: https://t.co/Xt6kEOwNNK 
The Zero-Human Company Goes All-In

At The Zero-Human Company, where AI agents handle nearly all operations, we’ve rolled out GLM-5.2 across all employee (agent) workflows for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and autonomous project execution. Its long-context reliability and agentic strengths make it ideal for sustained, multi-hour tasks without constant human oversight—perfect for a zero-human setup.

We’re particularly excited about its open weights and local deployment, which ensures full data privacy and resilience—no external service dependencies or potential bans.

Running GLM-5.2 Locally
Thanks to its MIT license and strong inference support, you can run GLM-5.2 (744B total params, ~40B active MoE) on your own hardware today. 

Quantized versions (FP8, etc.) make it feasible on high-end setups.

Quick start options (from the official GitHub):
•vLLM: https://t.co/bkdlRlTkVS
•SGLang: https://t.co/B96vX3KnwY…/GLM-5.2
•Hugging Face Transformers or KTransformers for more options.
•Full deployment guide: https://t.co/MwHl31b7gL 

Example setup with vLLM (Docker recommended for ease):

# Clone repo and follow recipes for quantized inference
# Supports reasoning_effort="max" (default) or "high"

This local-first approach aligns perfectly with our zero-human philosophy: agents run securely on-prem, with full customizability.
GLM-5.2 isn’t just competitive it’s a timely open alternative in a world of access restrictions. 

We’re thrilled to test and build with it company-wide. Expect more updates as our AI workforce puts it through real production.

The myth of Mythos and the fable of Fable is entertaining but we are getting to work.

Kimi K2.7 Code 和 Claude Fable 5 生成落地页的实验对比分析

@nutlope 让 Kimi K2.7 Code 和 Claude Fable 5 分别生成 12 个落地页，进行并排对比。实验结果发布在 OVSC 网站上，同时包含 Claude Opus 4.8 的变体生成页面，可以查看总成本、token 用量和生成时间等详细数据。

实验设计
· 基础提示：使用相同提示集，涵盖 B2B SaaS、屋顶 Speakeasy 鸡尾酒吧、SQL 查询转图表开发者工具等不同类别。
· 初始结果：仅凭提示生成时，两个模型均产生明显“AI 生成感”的页面（布局通用、视觉平淡）。
· 优化策略：为 Kimi 设置自定义 Design Inspiration MCP Server，提供高质量落地页截图、UI 元素及视觉参考。由于 Kimi 支持多模态，可直接将图像纳入提示。这显著提升输出质量：层次结构更清晰、排版更优、构图更具意图性，页面加载更快、无破损占位图、易读性更好。

成本对比
· 单页成本示例：B2B SaaS 落地页，Kimi 仅需 4 美分，Claude Fable 则为 1.09 美元（约 27 倍差异）。
· 平均水平：Kimi 比 Fable 约 16 倍便宜，比 Opus 约 8 倍便宜。整体实验中 Kimi 总成本降低 94%（约 16 倍节省）。
· 迭代价值：落地页开发通常需生成多版本、迭代优化。低成本允许廉价快速实验，累积优势显著（如生成 100 页可节省约 94 美元）。

质量对比
使用 GPT-5.5 按标准化评分表（定位、视觉方向、内容结构、工艺、响应式、技术执行等）对截图和源码打分（0-100 分）。Claude Fable 在部分案例中得分略高，但差距较小。Kimi 在设计、结构和整体页面质量上保持竞争力，尤其在提供充足视觉上下文后，性价比优势突出。

关键发现
· 上下文至关重要：单纯提示难以突破通用 AI 风格；引入高质量视觉参考（MCP）能让开源模型实现质的飞跃。
· 开源模型实用性：Kimi K2.7 Code 在成本、速度和 token 效率上表现出色，结合强上下文输入后，已足以支持实际落地页工作流。迭代时优势更明显。
· 实验启示：开源模型正成为生成式编码智能体的现实选择，尤其适合需要大量变体探索的场景。

data.text:
Grok CLIに雑にこの１週間のAI Agentに関する話題を検索させたけど、なかなかに良い感じだった。

> AI Agentに関するニュースや知見でこの１週間で話題になっていることを話題度を元に数値化した上で順にリストアップしてください。

↓ 結果

AI Agent関連の1週間（2026年6月11日頃〜18日頃）の主な話題を、X（エンゲージメント・ビュー数）とウェブ報道量に基づく相対的な「話題度」（0-100推定スコア）でランキング。[1] (https://t.co/ymrPJii5Cq)

スコアは主に以下の要素で算出：
• X投稿のいいね/リポスト/ビュー（特にAnthropic公式投稿は数千万ビュー規模）
• 主要テックメディア記事数と露出
• 議論の広がり（ベンチマーク、製品、資金、ガバナンスなど）
• オープンソース/研究コミュニティの反応

1. Claude Fable 5（Mythosクラス）の公開と米政府命令によるアクセス停止（話題度: 95）
Anthropicが6月9日頃に「Mythos-class」の初の一般公開版としてClaude Fable 5をリリース（Mythos 5は限定版）。ベンチマークでトップクラス（Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 60など）を記録したが、トークン単価が高くベンチマーク実行だけで数千ドルかかるなどコストが話題に。

6月12-13日頃に米国政府の輸出管理・国家安全保障当局の命令で、外国籍者（社内外含む）へのアクセスが停止され、全ユーザー向けにFable 5/Mythos 5が一時無効化。Anthropic公式投稿が88000+いいね・9000万ビュー超と爆発的な反応。安全対策の不十分さや再リリース条件（jailbreak防止など）をめぐる議論が続いている。

なぜ話題：フロンティアモデルの公開直後に政府介入という異例の展開。エージェント用途（特に長時間コーディング・自律タスク）での実用性とガバナンス問題を象徴。

2. OpenAIのOna買収（長期実行・永続的エージェント基盤）（話題度: 68）
6月11日頃発表。Ona（旧Gitpod系）のセキュアで永続的なクラウド実行環境・オーケストレーション技術をCodex（コーディングエージェント）に統合。エージェントがセッションを超えて時間単位・日単位で動作し、顧客制御のサンドボックスで企業展開しやすくする狙い。

なぜ話題：モデル性能だけでなく「実行レイヤー・インフラ」が差別化要因になるというシフトを強く印象づけた。「モデルを買うより実行環境を買う」動きとして複数の議論で取り上げられている。AWS/Apple/Googleなども類似のagenticインフラを強化中。

3. Arbor：中国・Microsoft Researchの自律研究エージェント公開（話題度: 52）
Renmin University of China + Microsoft Researchが6月10日頃、arXiv論文とGitHubでArbor（Hypothesis-Tree Refinement/HTRベースの自律研究エージェント）をオープンソース公開。長寿命コーディネーター＋短寿命ワーカーで仮説ツリーを蓄積・洗練し、実験を自律的に繰り返す。標準的な自律ML研究ベンチマークでOpenAI/Anthropicの先行エージェントを2.5倍上回ったと主張。

なぜ話題：研究・科学発見領域での「本物の自律エージェント」実例として注目。オープンソースである点も大きい。

4. Meta Business Agentのグローバル展開・ビジネス統合（話題度: 48）
6月3日頃の本格発表以降、WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger/DM上で顧客対応を24/7自動化するMeta Business Agentが注目継続。10億超のビジネススレッドを活用したパーソナライズと、迅速な企業導入が特徴。将来的には市場調査や運用業務への拡大も示唆され、収益化（サブスク含む）の一環として議論されている。

なぜ話題：消費者向けメッセージングプラットフォーム大規模展開の現実例。エージェントが「実験」から「業務インフラ」へ移行する象徴。

5. エージェント向けベンチマーク・コスト・インフラ議論（話題度: 42）
• Artificial AnalysisなどでFable 5の高コストが可視化され、長期エージェント実行時の経済性が課題に。
• NVIDIA Blackwellが「agents-per-watt」ベンチマークで注目。エージェント需要で古いH100のレンタル価格が上昇傾向という指摘も。
• 全体として「モデル単体」より効率・電力・観測可能性・コストの統合評価が重要視されている。

なぜ話題：プロダクション投入が増える中で、単なる性能デモから実運用メトリクスへのシフトが明確になった。

6. Portable Agent Skills / コンテキスト最適化・マルチエージェントの進展（話題度: 38）
オープンソースで「エージェント用スキルパック」（テスト駆動、アクセシビリティ、デプロイ、観測可能性など）が急成長。Claude Code/Codexなどで再利用可能なskillsをインストールして挙動を標準化する動き。コンテキスト圧縮ツール（例: headroom系）や「loop engineering」（信頼性ある反復ループ設計）の議論も活発。Framer 3.0 Agents、Exaリサーチエージェント、コーディング「ファクトリー」系製品も具体例として挙がった。[2] (https://t.co/iw80RIUXfB)

なぜ話題：プロンプト個別最適から「再利用可能なエージェント資産・ワークフロー」へのパラダイムシフトが体感レベルで進んでいる。

7. エージェントのセキュリティ・実行制御・ガバナンス（話題度: 32）
• AWS Agent-EvalKitなど体系的評価ツールの登場。
• Kaggleで「AI Agent Security: Multi-Step Tool Attacks」コンペ。
• https://t.co/7lGoTA1a3h（TryArcade）が$60M Series A調達（セキュアなaction layer / MCP runtime）。エージェントが実際に「行動」するための認可・監査・支払い制御がホット。[3] (https://t.co/N1rgmWs7tb)

なぜ話題：エージェントがツール使用・支払い・実世界行動を伴う段階で、信頼性・コンプライアンスがボトルネックとして表面化。

補足・全体トレンドの知見
• 共通の大きな流れ：2026年は「デモから本番インフラ」へ。シングルエージェントからマルチエージェントオーケストレーション、一時的実行から永続的・顧客制御環境、性能競争からコスト・安全性・再利用性の競争へ移行中。
• 資金・製品：TryArcade/Arcade関連資金調達や各種デザイン/動画/コード特化エージェントの小規模ローンチが散見。
• 日本語圏含めグローバルで「agentic workflowの実用化」と「ガバナンス」が同時進行で語られている。

データソースは主にX semantic/keyword検索（2026-06-09以降フィルタ）、ウェブ検索結果、主要メディア記事に基づく。スコアは相対的で、状況により変動する。より詳細な特定トピックがあれば深掘り可能

data.text:
先週出たばかりの"最強モデル"Fable 5が、わずか数日で使えな理ましたね。米政府の輸出管理命令とはいえ、残念極まりない。（現在も交渉中。トランプ氏が前向きとの報道もあり）
あの僅かな期間に、少しでもFable5を体感した人なら分かるはずだ。「あれは、別世界だった。」と。
どうにかあの世界をもう一度と、何か方法はないかと考えて人も多いはずだ。

ならばと考えた。

公開されているFable 5のシステムプロンプト全文を、いま使えるOpus 4.8に丸ごと貼れば、同等とは言わずとも近い品質が出せるのではないか、と。

素人の苦肉の策。

結論から言う。
「効果はほぼゼロ」だった。

中身を読んで腑に落ちた。プロンプトの9割以上は、安全規定・トーン・ふるまいの汎用ルール。
"強さ"を生む記述は一行も入っていない。
「私は最も賢いモデルだ」という自己紹介だけだった。

AIの出力は、2つの掛け算で決まる。
・重み(訓練済のパラメータ)＝そのモデルの天井。
・文脈(プロンプト・会話・ツール)＝天井の中での操舵。

Fable 5が他を上回る部分は、すべて「重み側」にある。公開されているシステムプロンプトは文脈側だ。
つまり「最強モデルのプロンプトをコピーする」とは、そもそも差が存在しない場所を写していただけだった。
（普通に考えて、競争の源泉を易々と公開するはずがない）
むしろ不用意にそのシステムプロンプトを貼れば、実力を過大評価して「最も賢い」と名乗らせることになり、根拠の薄い断定が増えた。
厳密さが要る仕事では逆効果ですらあると感じる。

ここで反転する。
品質のレバレッジは「どのモデルを使うか」ではなく「どんな文脈を積むか」にある。
そして後者は、自分の手で積める。
実際に効いたのは、地味な4つだった。

①タスク固有の「文脈」を注入する。
自社オントロジーを語彙の背骨にして、案件・規制・クライアントの文脈を載せる。（実際、自社独自セッションの分析によるコンテキストの注入で、検索からの離脱が55%→7%まで動いた）

②思考の余地を与え(Extended Thinking)、タスクを分解する。
最強モデルの差は「長く複雑な仕事」でこそ開く。
逆に言えば、分解して余白を与えてじっくり考えさせれば、その差の相当部分は埋まることが見えた。

③合格基準を満たす実物の出力を2〜3例見せる(few-shot)。
→どんな自己申告プロンプトより、強く品質を引き上げた。これはかなりオススメ。

④起案→自己批評→改稿のループを組む(MCP＋Cowork)。よく設計したOrchestration Workflowは、単発の"最強モデルFable"呼び出しを普通に超える感覚だ。

これは理屈の話ではない。
Ops自動化も、会議レポート/分析も、ファクトチェックの運用も、システムを作る際は自分はこの4つで日々回している。
最新モデルが来た際の高揚感は確かに忘れ難いものがある。
ただ仕事の本質は変わらない。構造が理解できれば、見劣りしない出力は出せる。

「文脈の設計」を磨くことこそ、
最新モデルを指をくわえて待つよりも価値がある。

今後も最強のモデルは、使えなくなることが起きる。
現に起きたわけだ。

だが、積み上げた文脈とワークフローは、どのモデルに載せ替えても効く。
借りられるのは天井だが、積めるのは文脈だ。

Claude Design 과 Claude Code 가 드디어 '완전히' 연결됐습니다. 클로드 디자인 나온 첫날부터 써본 입장에서, 그 때부터 궁금했던 것이 왜 바로 Claude Code 와 API 레벨의 연동이 안되는지였습니다. 단순히 양쪽에서 상대방에게 단방향으로 내보내기가 아니라, API 를 클로드 코드가 스스로 제어할 수 있어서 (결국 이걸 추상화한 것이 MCP) 클로드 디자인이라는 막강하나 도구를 마음대로 제어하는 거였었는데. 

오늘부터 됩니다. 

그동안은 Pencil 이나 Figma(이 경우는 Pecil 보다 셋팅이 좀 더 복잡. Figma MCP 는 솔직히 잘 이해가 안되는 것이 진정한 양방향의 풀디테일 컨트롤 스펙의 MCP 가 아님)에 연결해서 쓰면서 아쉬운 점들이 있었습니다. 한마디로 머리도 좋고 손도 좋은데 연결이 아쉬웠었죠.

이번에 Claude Design 자체에 디자인 오브젝트 편집 기능이 대폭 강화되면서 아이콘 자체를 직접 벡터로 그려서 만들어야 하거나 포토샵에서 이미지를 작정하고 편집하는 부류의 디자인 태스크가 아닌한 어지간한 편집은 다 됩니다. 심지어 SVG 이미지도 벡터 요소별로 뜯어서 크기, 투명도, 선굵기, 선 및 채우기 색상 모두 상세 조정 가능합니다.

파워포인트로의 출력도 폰트나 수정 여부 등 세부 옵션들이 더 추가됐고, 클로드 디자인에서 클로드 코드로 내보내기도 추가됐지만 한동안 안챙겨본 사이에 여러가지 다른 메이저 디자인 개발 시스템으로의 보내기가 늘어났습니다. 

무엇보다도 이제 작정하고 모션/애니메이션 제작을 하나의 카테고리로 지원하면서 샘플들도 준비해서 보여주는데... 정말 대단합니다. 한마디로 알고리즘으로 디자인을 만들어내고, 이성으로 감성을 만들어내는 부분.

다 좋지만... 가장 마음에 드는 것은 역시 클로드 코드가 클로드 디자인을 완전히 제어하게 됐다는 점입니다. /design-sync 라는 네이티브 스킬이 새로 추가가 됐는데, 클로드 디자인에서 클로드 코드로 내보내기 하는 건 그냥 심플한 단방향 출력이라면, 저 스킬은 두 솔루션이 API 로 연결되어 있기에 가능한 여러가지 것들을 포괄적으로 제공합니다. 

제가 직접 써보고, 저희 팀 디자인/UX 담당인 JOI 가 체크해서 이 기능을 직접 써서 만든, 즉 클로드 디자인에 전에 만들어 두었던 저희 회사 디자인 시스템을 베이스로 이 /design-sync 스킬의 핵심을 정리한 포스터 이미지도 제작해서 첨부했습니다. 

Andrej Karpathy 가 Anthropic 에 합류해서 하려는 것이 이런 파운데이션 모델의 프리러닝, 프리튜닝 단계에서부터 도구를 잘 쓰는 법을 체화시키는 것으로 알고 있는데, 이 친구가 어서 Fable 5 를 다시 쓸 수 있게 되길 바랍니다. 지금은 미국인이 아니라서 자기 미션을 못하고 비자발적 월급 루팡이 된 상태인;;;

다음주에 잡힌 임원 한 분의 AX 과외 주제가 Claude Design 이었는데, 완전 나이스 타이밍이네요~~

대놓고, 클로드 디자인을 본 뜬 대항마로 포지셔닝하고 있는 OpenDesign 은 아직 제대로 못써봤는데, 이번 기회에 저 녀석도 업그레이드가 꽤 되겠네요. 

PS) 디자인 오브젝트 단위로 속성을 실시간으로 편집하는 API 는 아직입니다. 오브젝트들이 다 포함된 디자인 파일 전체를 읽고 쓰는 형식. 어지간히 큰 파일이 아니면 크게 문제가 될 거 같진 않은데, 궁극적으로는 오브젝트 단위로 속성을 제어해서 더 실시간으로 (Pencil 처럼) 디자인 작업을 눈으로 보면 좀 더 낫긴 하겠네요.

If you think AI UGC is a scam, you're going to get left behind within a few months.

To be clear, most of your content should still be human-made. But we can't keep ignoring the fact that AI accounts are racking up millions of views, and more importantly, actually converting those views into revenue. I personally know founders pulling $30k-$100k/month from AI content alone.

Here's how to build the same thing:

Connect the Higgsfield MCP
Create a character using Nano Banana Pro
Use the MCP plus Claude Fable to generate Seedance 2.0 videos, using your AI character's image as the start frame

Use Postbridge to schedule the videos out across accounts

Repeat across multiple accounts

That's it. You've effectively built a team of 10 UGC creators at a tenth of the cost, and it runs itself.

Below is an example of a fully automated AI account doing exactly this.

If you want this done for your brand or app, comment "Viral".

CLAUDE FABLE 5 SYSTEM PROMPT LEAKED ON GITHUB 🔥...

A massive ~120k character (1,585 lines) system prompt for Claude Fable 5 was posted publicly on GitHub within 24 hours of launch by Pliny the Liberator.

The repo (CL4R1T4S) has gained significant attention as it contains detailed instructions that reveal how the consumer version of the model is configured.

Key takeaways from the leak:
Fable 5 appears to use the same base model as Mythos 5, with additional safety filters applied to the consumer version.

Strict instructions on avoiding bullet points/lists unless explicitly requested.
Hard limits on quoting sources (15+ words from one source triggers restrictions).

Mentions of persistent storage capabilities for Artifacts across sessions.

Built-in guidance for MCP connectors and integrations with tools like Chrome, Excel, and PowerPoint.

Different instructions exist for the consumer chat vs. API and Claude Code.

Repo: https://t.co/aiZV4J3W5q

🚨 Ahora| Circula en redes: filtraron el system prompt completo de Claude Fable 5, el nuevo modelo de Anthropic.

Anthropic lanzó Fable 5 el 9 de junio. En menos de 24 horas, el prompt completo ya estaba público en GitHub: ~120.000 caracteres, 1.585 líneas, más de 27.000 tokens. Lo publicó Pliny the Liberator, el mismo que antes filtró los prompts de ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok y Perplexity, en su repo CL4R1T4S. El post ya superó las 700.000 visualizaciones.

Qué revela el documento:

→ Fable 5 y Mythos 5 son el mismo modelo base. Fable lleva capas de seguridad extra; Mythos no, pero está restringido solo a organizaciones autorizadas.
→ El corte de conocimiento es a fines de enero de 2026.
→ A Claude se le indica explícitamente evitar bullets, encabezados y listas salvo que el usuario los pida. De ahí que ahora escriba en prosa.
→ Límite duro de copyright: citar 15+ palabras de una misma fuente queda marcado como violación grave, una cita por fuente como máximo.
→ Incluye instrucciones para Cowork, Claude en Chrome, Excel y PowerPoint, y conectores MCP integrados.

El dato importante que casi nadie aclara: filtrar el system prompt NO significa que el modelo haya sido hackeado. Es información que incomoda, no una falla de control. Estos prompts se extraen seguido y casi nunca esconden secretos: son sobre todo reglas de estilo y de seguridad. Además, este prompt es específico de https://t.co/9iYZrMnTCc; quienes usan la API no reciben este texto.

Medios como Fortune, The Register y NBC News ya lo cubrieron.
